about.title: About me
about.text1: Right now I am commuting between two places. In Lüneburg I study Digital Media with Business Psychology as a minor at Leuphana University, and recently I also started International Business Administration & Entrepreneurship.
about.text2: In Hamburg I have been working as a working student at a web design agency since 2025, where I am responsible for SEO. With my own clients whom I look after every month.
about.text3: Over the next few months, I want to bring these two areas closer together: what I’m learning in school about technology, media, data, people, and AI, and the practical work I do every day at the agency. That’s why I’m open to internships that allow me to explore new, relevant fields where I can put my current knowledge to the test and continue to build on it.
about.marketTitle: Side job at the weekly market
work.howText: Originally, I was looking for a working student position in marketing. That’s how I ended up at a job interview with Homepage Helden. It turned out there was no longer a need to fill the marketing position after all. But I must have made a good impression on the HR manager, because she offered me a position in support instead. I started there with no prior experience and worked my way up step by step. What I was missing, though, was a field that I really enjoyed and where I could thrive. I found it rather by chance in the agency’s SEO team. The team had just been formed at that time. Since then, I’ve been learning from my colleagues in a small team and continuing to develop my professional skills.
work.whatText: Since 2025 I have been working as a working student at a web design agency in Hamburg, where I am responsible for search engine optimisation.
work.task1: Looking after my own clients, with a monthly report
work.task2: Technical optimisation: loading times, structure, indexing
work.task3: Content optimisation: keywords, texts, page structure
work.learnedText: Professionally, my work-study position has helped me learn a lot, especially in SEO, AI and web programming in general, including working with systems like TYPO3, WordPress, and Statamic. And that learning never stops; every project brings new knowledge. But the personal side is just as important to me. I’ve gotten a sense of what it means to be part of the working world. On top of that, working as part of a team has allowed me to learn a lot from experienced colleagues.
work.toolsHint: 11 in daily use · tap for details
tools.semrush: One of two tools for retrieving SEO-related data such as search volume and rankings. | Third Party
tools.sistrix: Overview of the most important SEO metrics for a selected website. | Third Party
tools.seranking: The second tool for retrieving SEO-related data such as search volume and rankings. | Third Party
tools.searchconsole: Overview of the most important SEO metrics for a selected website. | First Party from Google
tools.datastudio: To create monthly reports (to-do lists or keyword ranking trends via the API, etc.)
tools.googleads: I have less prior experience with this tool than with the others. I've only tested it in my personal time on my father's company's website.
tools.claude: Claude is the AI that I primarily use for both personal and academic and professional purposes, and I've been using it for quite some time now.
tools.chatgpt: Of course, I used ChatGPT at first. But now I use it less often thanks to Claude. If at all, it's just for generating images.
tools.gemini: I also use Gemini, if at all, for image generation. However, NotebookLM really stands out as a positive option, especially in a university setting.
tools.web: I basically deal with HTML, CSS & JS all the time at work. But as an SEO, a basic understanding, especially of HTML, is enough for me. There are developers who specialize in CSS and other technical implementations.
tools.excel: I also use Excel a lot at work. However, I usually stick to the standard use cases.
uni.mainHoped: Originally, I wanted to focus primarily on business psychology. Since I had to choose a second major, I decided on digital media. I was hoping this would give me practical insights that would be helpful in an increasingly digital world.
uni.mainSoFar: Basically, I'm very satisfied with my studies. At the same time, I realize how much my job has added to my experience. It shows me different perspectives, and I can directly compare what I learn in school with what I experience on the job.
uni.mainLearned: In terms of my interests, I was particularly drawn to the technical courses, such as a Python module from the second semester. Lately, though, I’ve also been particularly drawn to modules related to AI. The topic is so incredibly groundbreaking and will continue to revolutionize our society in many areas. That’s why I want to delve into it as deeply as possible. And as I said, I also apply the knowledge I gain from my university modules to other areas of my life, such as my free time or at work.
uni.additionalHoped: I’d especially like to broaden my horizons in the field of economics, since I’m not focusing on it enough right now. For one thing, economics is another area of interest for me. For another, it’s knowledge that will pay off later on, especially if I ever want to run my own business.
uni.additionalSoFar: Since I'm just getting started with my studies, I'll be able to add more to this section over time.
